- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.15) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.15), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) with negative sentiment, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overconfidence.  
- If model shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive falling forecasts) with positive sentiment, increase forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% for next 5–10 days; if < -1.5σ, increase by 10–15%.  
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (±0.15+ in last 5 days), reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to avoid overfitting.
